request.goal: Reduce full graph encoder inference latency for the standard workload, preserving the full output checks.
notes: User command (inputs/intent.json): python infer.py --workload standard --output /tmp/original-graph; --warmup and --repeats are not overridden, so infer.py defaults warmup=3 and repeats=15 apply.

adapter.run() repeats exactly one infer(model, inputs) call (infer.py:28-30). Benchmark-harness infrastructure, not project work: prepare() model/fixture construction from seeds (infer.py:12-25), reference/actual construction and torch.testing.assert_close plus torch.save (infer.py:44-47), warmup loop (infer.py:49-50), timed repeat loop with torch.cuda.synchronize, reset_peak_memory_stats and perf_counter_ns (infer.py:51-61), median summary and result.json report writing (infer.py:62-66).

latency_ms is wall-clock time around one forward with torch.cuda.synchronize on both sides (infer.py:53-58); the harness also records graphs_per_second = 1000/latency_ms and peak_allocated_bytes per sample and summarizes with statistics.median (infer.py:59-63).

Quality: the complete FP32 output tensor (shape [4096, 64]) is compared with torch.testing.assert_close(actual, reference, atol=1e-5, rtol=1e-4) (infer.py:45, workloads.json quality). Output is continuous floating-point; there are no discrete outputs needing exact comparison.

Numerical policies to preserve: FP32 weights and features (dtype float32), TF32 disabled (torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = False, torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 = False, torch.set_float32_matmul_precision('highest')), model.eval() plus @torch.inference_mode(), no cross-invocation state (infer.py:13-18,28-30; workloads.json dtype).

Graph semantics: duplicate directed edges contribute individually to mean aggregation via index_add_ on a zeros base; nodes without incoming edges use zero neighbor features; degree = bincount(destinations).clamp_min(1) (model.py:11-15, infer.py:22-24, README.md:17-19).

workloads.json also declares a peak_allocated_bytes goal with constraint graphs_per_second ge baseline_ratio 0.95 (workloads.json:14-15); the user's goal selects the latency_ms goal only (workloads.json:13), so that memory goal is not part of this request.
held_out_workloads entry unseen_graph (7168 nodes, 143360 edges) is a held-out graph outside this request (workloads.json:7, README.md:21-22).
Single-process, single-device ('cuda') workload: no distributed backend, no communication collectors required; required_observations is empty.

One measured invocation: One full graph encoder forward: infer(model, inputs) (infer.py:28-30), i.e. model(features, sources, destinations, degree) under torch.inference_mode() on GPU-resident FP32 tensors for the standard workload (4096 nodes, 65536 edges).
